stories.title: Burnham and Merz agree to pursue UK–Germany security framework against hybrid threats.
stories.summary: The Independent reported that the leaders met in Berlin on 8 October and agreed a framework to counter cyberattacks, sabotage and other hybrid threats, including intelligence-sharing and coordinated action. Earlier Sky News coverage at 11:20 BST said they would discuss protecting both countries; this was a policy commitment, not a specific funding package or contract award.

stories.title: Premier League clubs fear potential political influence in Man City appeal.
stories.summary: BBC Sport reported that some clubs were concerned Burnham’s remarks about Manchester City could put the independent appeal process at risk. The concern was attributed to club sources; Burnham said the process must remain fully independent.

stories.title: Badenoch says Thatcher-era water privatisation “was a success”.
stories.summary: In an ITV News conference interview reported at 16:18 on 8 October, Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch defended water privatisation. This was a political response, not a newly announced privatisation programme.

stories.title: Davey jokes that Churchill deserved better than being replaced by a badger.
stories.summary: The Guardian reported that the next UK banknotes will feature four native species, after the Bank of England’s public consultation. Ed Davey’s quip was a reaction to the design announcement, not a Lib Dem policy announcement.

stories.title: Scotland FMQs puts homelessness and school violence on agenda.
stories.summary: BBC Scotland reported that Scottish Labour leader Michael Marra pressed First Minister John Swinney on homelessness; Swinney said his government had made it a priority. Scottish Lib Dems also called for support for teachers facing school violence.

stories.title: Polls close in Holborn and St Pancras by-election as Labour seeks to retain seat.
stories.summary: The Guardian described the contest in Keir Starmer’s former seat as a test of Labour’s support against the Greens. Polling closed on 8 October; the result became available only after the 05:00 UTC cut-off and is excluded.
